ותניא, 21a.4: R' Yehuda -- no doors, only oxen
the sages of the Ohalot mishnah's first clause (ורבנן, 21a.1)

props.gloss_en: one who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah has not fulfilled his obligation
R' Yehuda: we were accustomed to sleep under the bed before the elders, and they said nothing
Shmuel interpreted the mishnah as speaking of a bed ten [tefachim] high
a hole bored by water or creeping things or eaten out by salt, a course of stones, a pile of beams -- forms a tent over impurity
R' Yehuda: any tent not made by man is not a tent

the stam: R' Yehuda derives 'tent'-'tent' from the Tabernacle -- 'a man who dies in a tent' (Bamidbar 19:14), 'and he spread the tent over the Tabernacle' (Shemot 40:19): as there by man, so here by man
the stam: and the sages -- the repeated 'tent', 'tent' amplifies

the Para mishnah: courtyards in Jerusalem built over the rock with a hollow beneath, for fear of a grave in the depths; they brought oxen with doors on their backs, the children sat on them holding stone cups; at the Shiloach they went down into the water and filled them
the Para mishnah's first view: at the Shiloach the children descended into the water and filled the cups
R' Yosei: each child lowered [the cup] from his place and filled it, because of a grave in the depths
the baraita, R' Yehuda: they did not bring doors -- only oxen
R' Elazar (via Rav Dimi): R' Yehuda concedes [that a tent not made by man is a tent] where it is a fistbreadth
the baraita: R' Yehuda concedes regarding caves and rock clefts
Abaye: [R' Yehuda means] they did not NEED to bring doors
Rava: they brought no doors at all, because a child grows over-confident on one and may put out his head or a limb and become impure from a grave in the depths
the baraita, R' Yehuda: no doors at all, because the child grows over-confident and may put out his head; rather Egyptian oxen with broad bellies
the stam: a bed is different, since it is made for [use] on top of it
R' Elazar (via Ravin): oxen are different, since they shelter the shepherds from the sun and from the rain
Rava: rather, oxen are different, since [their bodies] are made to protect their own innards
Rava's verse: 'with skin and flesh You clothed me, and with bones and sinews You covered me' (Iyov 10:11)
R' Yehuda, as the stam cites him: we require a sukkah that is a permanent dwelling
the stam: R' Yehuda follows his reasoning -- the bed is a temporary dwelling and the sukkah a permanent tent, and a temporary tent does not negate a permanent one
R' Shimon, as the stam cites him: he too requires a sukkah that is a permanent dwelling
one master (R' Shimon): a temporary tent does negate a permanent tent
and the other master (R' Yehuda): a temporary tent does not negate a permanent tent
the stam: on this they disagree -- whether a temporary tent negates a permanent one

the repeated 'ohel' amplifies: any shelter forms a tent, even one not made by man -- stated by the stam as the sages' reading

supports.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: ומודה רבי יהודה בשקיפין ובנקיקי הסלעים

answered_by.gloss_en: Rav Dimi in R' Elazar's name: R' Yehuda concedes for a fistbreadth (= p_elazar_modeh_egrof)

answered_by.gloss_en: no doors at all, lest the over-confident child put out his head and be defiled (= p_rava_daato_gasa)

objections.gloss_en: והרי מטה דיש בה כמה אגרופים, ותנן רבי יהודה אומר: נוהגים היינו שהיינו ישנים תחת המטה! -- a bed has several fistbreadths, yet R' Yehuda does not treat it as a tent

אלא אמר רבא: oxen are made to protect their own innards, שנאמר עור ובשר תלבישני (= p_rava_bnei_meayim)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, מטה נמי — הואיל ומגינה על מנעלים וסנדלים שתחתיה! -- unanswered; Rava's אלא replaces R' Elazar's distinction
